title: Introduce Response Guardian: streaming JSON-schema checkpoints, toolcall snapshotting, and OpenAI-compat bridge
author: Anika Patel
description:
Summary: Adds a new runtime component called Response Guardian that verifies structured output against JSON schemas at deterministic streaming checkpoints, captures a compact toolcall snapshot to allow safe downstream tool execution, and exposes a small OpenAI-compatibility shim so OpenAI-conformant clients can opt into strict/lenient semantics.
Motivation: We've seen recurring production incidents where streamed outputs diverge from declared schemas after long token sequences or when tool calls mutate state. Customers with strict contracts need early, actionable validation signals instead of waiting for final output validation failures. This PR implements checkpoint-based validation (low-overhead) and a toolcall snapshot so callers can either block tool invocations on soft failures or proceed with best-effort fallbacks.
Design:
- Response Guardian: a middleware-like component in the serving runtime that registers schema checkpoints at configurable token offsets and on toolcall boundaries. Each checkpoint performs an incremental JSON-schema validation pass limited to the new delta tokens and cached object roots.
- Toolcall snapshotting: before invoking user-configured tools, the runtime captures a canonical, compact snapshot of the partially-parsed JSON structure and a provenance token. Tools receive the snapshot instead of raw stream fragments; after tool return the Guardian reconciles edits and validates the merged object.
- Failure modes: two configurable policies are supported: "strict" (failclosed: reject the stream and surface an error immediately) and "graceful" (failopen: emit a structured validation warning event and continue; final validation still enforced).
- OpenAI-compat bridge: supports legacy clients via a query param (response_mode=compat) or header (X-RW-Resp-Mode: compat/strict/graceful). In compat mode, the Guardian maps Redwood error codes to OpenAI-style error objects and preserves streaming boundary behavior expected by OpenAI SDKs.
Behavior & contract:
- Checkpoints are registered automatically when a response_format includes a JSON schema or when tool-calling is used. Users can configure additional checkpoints per route.
- Checkpoint validation is incremental and bounded (configurable max nodes checked per checkpoint) so CPU overhead is predictable.
- When strict mode triggers, the runtime returns a structured error payload that includes the checkpoint id, validation errors (flattened), and a resume token suggestion where applicable.
- Toolcall snapshots are canonicalized and HMAC-signed for integrity; snapshot tokens are single-use and expire in 30s by default.
Compatibility & rollout:
- Default route behavior remains unchanged for customers who don't opt into structured response_format.
- New behavior is behind a feature flag and enabled by default for beta testers and enterprise tenants that requested schema SLOs.
- Migration notes: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) are updated to accept the snapshot object instead of raw stream chunks; the server will also accept legacy hooks and convert transparently while the SDKs upgrade.
Testing & CI:
- Unit tests: schema validator fuzz harness, snapshot canonicalizer tests, checkpoint scheduling.
- Integration tests: end-to-end stream with toolcall mock, simulated flaky tool returns, strict vs graceful policy matrix.
- Load tests: microbenchmarked checkpoint overhead across typical sequence length distributions (see perf section below).
Checklist:
- [x] Runtime component and API surface implemented
- [x] SDK bindings (Python + TS) updated for snapshot consumption
- [x] Docs: Console docs and API reference added
- [x] Perf benchmarks updated
- [x] Security review for snapshot signing and expiry
